Let’s dive into Chapter 5—Building Consistency and Intentionality in Spiritual Practice.
Here’s something a lot of us need to hear: developing a steady awareness of God’s presence doesn’t just happen on its own. Just like any real relationship, it takes intention, effort, and a bit of consistency. The point isn’t to chain yourself to some rigid routine. It’s to build habits that keep that connection alive, day in and day out.
Consistency actually starts with the little things. Instead of overhauling your whole life overnight, try weaving small moments of awareness into your regular day. Think about it—maybe you set aside a few quiet minutes for reflection, or you use a sticky note on your desk to remind you to pause and check in with God. Even dedicating a simple, everyday activity—like making your morning coffee or taking a walk—as an act of devotion can make a huge difference.
One of the easiest ways to look at spiritual practice is like a series of gentle check-ins. Imagine how you’d touch base with a close friend or family member—those little moments, spread through the day, help build a steady rhythm of relationship. Over time, these check-ins become as natural as breathing.
So, what tools can actually help you build that kind of consistency? Here are a few ideas:
You could set up simple cues or reminders—a quick note, a phone alarm, or even a meaningful symbol in your space—to nudge you toward moments of awareness.
Or, try linking spiritual reflection with things you already do, like sipping your coffee in the morning or enjoying a daily stroll.
And at the end of the day, why not take a few minutes to look back? Notice where you felt connected, or where you missed those moments, and just talk honestly with God about it.
Now, intentionality means making choices about what really matters. Life’s noisy, and it’s so easy to let spiritual things slide to the very edge of your schedule. But when you decide to protect that time—to keep it front and center—your relationship with God starts to shift from an afterthought to a core part of who you are.
Flexibility is key, though. Life throws curveballs, and sometimes routines just don’t stick. That’s okay. The goal isn’t to be perfect, but to keep showing up—even if how you do it needs to change now and then. What matters most is that spirit of connection, not the exact form it takes.
Over time, these new habits form a solid foundation. You start to feel God’s presence more deeply, and your relationship grows stronger and steadier. Of course, there’ll be challenges and days when things don’t go as planned. But each morning brings a new chance to begin again.
And here’s the heart of it—it’s not about trying to earn God’s favor, or racking up spiritual achievements. It’s about saying yes to an invitation. Walking through life with a constant companion, sharing every moment, and discovering the real joy that comes from genuine interaction.
